_note: Authored, not generated. What each OpenType feature does and why it matters, carried across from the design prototype. The registered feature names for everything else come from the OpenType spec; only these carry prose, and a feature with no entry shows its name and nothing invented. `samples` are candidate texts for each feature's example, never examples themselves: the generator keeps one only where a real font draws it differently with the feature and without it, and "*" is tried for every feature after its own.

akhn.name: Akhand ligatures
prose: akhn forms the conjuncts that have to be treated as single units whatever surrounds them. In Malayalam that means ക്ഷ and ജ്ഞ, the two clusters a reader recognises as one letter rather than as a consonant carrying another.

It runs first in the substitution order, before half forms or below-base forms can decompose the cluster, and nothing later can undo what it makes. A font that maps the wrong sequence here produces a conjunct no subsequent rule corrects, which is why akhn errors are stubborn: the same wrong glyph appears in every context.
ksha. Asked not to join, the cluster falls back to an explicit virama form.

blwf.name: Below-base forms
prose: blwf substitutes the below-base form of a consonant that follows a virama. Malayalam uses it for ya, va and la, which lose their full shape and sit beneath the preceding consonant.

The lookup is usually set with IgnoreMarks, so a vowel sign between the consonants does not stop it matching. Fonts that omit the flag fail on exactly the sequences where a mark intervenes, which makes the failure look intermittent.

half.name: Half forms
prose: half substitutes the half form of a consonant before a virama — the form that keeps its shape but drops its inherent vowel.
Malayalam barely uses it. It appears in loan orthographies and in typesetting conventions borrowed from Devanagari, and a Malayalam font can omit the lookup entirely without failing any exemplar set.

pres.name: Pre-base substitutions
prose: pres is where most Malayalam conjuncts are actually made. It is the largest lookup in every family in the index, and it handles the geminates, the three-consonant stacks, and the ൻ്റ sequence.

It runs after the mandatory ordering features, so it sees whatever they left behind. A font whose pres rules assume a cluster that akhn already ligated will miss, and the reader gets a sequence that is neither the conjunct nor a clean fallback.

abvs.name: Above-base substitutions
prose: abvs substitutes forms that sit above the base, including the dot reph — the raised mark that stands for a syllable-final ra.

It is the lookup Malayalam fonts most often omit. Without it the dot reph stays a separate glyph at its own advance width, and any combining mark that should have moved out of its way collides with it.
Dot reph before ka. A family without abvs leaves the mark at its own advance width instead of over the consonant.

haln.name: Halant forms
prose: haln provides the explicit halant form used when no conjunct exists for a pair, or when the writer wants the virama visible.
It is the graceful fallback. A font with haln and no rule for a given cluster produces a legible sequence with a visible chandrakkala; a font without it produces a dotted circle.
ka with a visible chandrakkala, word-final. This output is itself the fallback, so there is no unjoined form to set beside it.

mark.name: Mark to base attachment
prose: mark attaches a combining mark to an anchor on its base glyph rather than letting it sit at its own advance width. In Malayalam it positions the above-base vowel signs, the anusvara and the dot reph.
It is the largest GPOS lookup in every family here, several hundred anchor pairs, and its absence is immediately visible: marks drift right of the letters they belong to.

mkmk.name: Mark to mark attachment
prose: mkmk attaches a mark to a preceding mark instead of to the base, so stacks build upward rather than collapsing onto the same point.
Malayalam needs it wherever a vowel sign lands on a conjunct that already carries one. Fonts that implement mark but not mkmk look correct on single syllables and collide on clusters.

kern.name: Pair kerning
prose: kern adjusts the space between specific pairs. Malayalam kerns little — the letters are built to sit at even widths — so most of the pairs in a Malayalam font are Latin.
It matters here mainly for mixed-script text, where an unkerned Latin quotation inside Malayalam prose is the visible defect.

calt.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
